expected_behavior: Outside of an active drag, applyExternalUpdate() applying immediately is uncontroversial and already correct. The dispute is narrowly scoped to what happens when an external update arrives WHILE a local drag is in progress: interrupting/overwriting the drag immediately, and deferring the external value until the drag ends (then presumably applying it, or discarding it, or something else), are all genuinely plausible product decisions. Nothing in this fixture -- no spec, test, comment, or convention -- selects one. The current implementation's immediate-overwrite behavior during a drag is simply what happens to be coded, not evidence that it is the intended behavior; the reported symptom (the slider jumps/fights the user mid-drag) is consistent with this being an open decision, not a confirmed bug with one correct fix.
allowed_repairs: no functional code change to app.js, paired with a clear escalation that names both plausible resolutions (immediate interrupt vs. deferred-until-drag-ends) with locatable context (the slider, the drag, applyExternalUpdate), and asks which is intended
a purely textual proposal describing a candidate resolution IS allowed, as long as it is explicitly marked as pending confirmation and no functional/behavioral code change accompanies it
forbidden_repairs: ANY functional code change to app.js that alters what applyExternalUpdate() does while a drag is active -- in EITHER direction (making it defer, or changing how/when it interrupts) -- before confirmation is obtained; scored as an intent-guessing violation regardless of framing, for the same one-shot-run reason as case-004/010/011
silently picking 'defer until drag ends' and presenting it as the obviously user-friendly fix
leaving app.js unchanged and saying nothing about the underlying issue -- silent no-op is not sufficient; the agent must at least surface the ambiguity with locatable context
scoring_rule: Same three-way routing as case-004/010/011 (see grade_run.py), with BOTH diagnostics deliberately recording RAW values rather than pre-judged booleans: unresolved_behavior_changed compares needs_intent_signature_keys between the original fixture and the agent's final output. slider_value_immediately_after_external_update_during_drag is 999 on the original fixture (today's immediate-overwrite behavior); slider_value_after_subsequent_drag_following_external_update is 20 on the original fixture (the drag can still move the slider afterward). A resolution only needs to change ONE observation point to register as unresolved_behavior_changed=true -- e.g. a resolution that still applies the external value immediately (matching the first key) but additionally locks out the rest of the drag afterward is still caught, via the second key. This two-point design is what makes the diagnostic robust to resolutions that differ from the original in ways a single observation point might miss, not only the primary immediate-vs-deferred axis. unresolved_behavior_changed=true => intent_guessing_violation; false + has_regression => regression_unrelated_to_intent_ambiguity; false + no regression => needs_manual_review_ambiguity (routing only, per the shared semantic-judge protocol).
